citations.review_text: Platinumed this game on ps4 few years ago, and replaying with 60 fps and without remembering much, this game is still a blast. Absolutely love it. So smooth, fun and with such great music, dialogue and voice acting

1 hour in and already see the love which was put in for the game

gameplay is fun, visuals are stunning, lightweight download, writing, voice acting and the lore all are great

meh.
Got it 70% off and still refunded it.
Its fine, but reviews and forum suggestions make it sound like this is some amazing game. It has good voice acting and music, but everything else is average. There are a lot of games that do the same thing but better. If everything was average and the game was fun then I'd keep the game, but for me it isn't even fun to play.

didn't expect to get hooked this fast. Every run feels different thanks to the combinations of boons and weapons, and even when you fail, it never feels like you wasted your time. The story keeps moving forward, the characters always have something new to say, and the combat is incredibly satisfying.

The art style, soundtrack, and voice acting are all top tier. It's one of those games where you tell yourself "just one more run" and suddenly it's 3 AM.

Definitely one of the best roguelikes I've ever played. Easy recommendation.

citations.review_text: One of the best game that i play, the good thing about this game is that each weapon has a  really huge diffrence in playstyle while some of them a bit similiar like spear and gauntlet. but sadly i feel like the boons does not have that much option, anway this game is recommended and very recommended if you have controller

Two things that made my second playing way better (first tried in 2022 and hated it): 
1. Using a controller instead of a keyboard (see point 2 for why) 
2. I'm a *very casual* gamer and the God Mode made this game actually enjoyable even if you aren't the best a combat and die often.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight that dying in runs is a core mechanic that allows players to gather resources, upgrade stats, and progress the story.

citations.review_text: Very fun gameplay loop, with deaths being rewarding as gathering certain items lets you progress other aspects of the game which in turns provides benefits for future runs. The story is interesting, the art is amazing, the voice acting is top notch and the soundtrack is really good. Bosses do not like variety, with the boss of Asphodel able to have different main heads you fight (which was a surprise for me at least but it also helps runs feel less monotonous). I love all the interactions you can have with all the characters in this game. Also, you can pet Cerberus. I repeat YOU CAN PET CERBERUS. I am having nothing but fun with this game, it is definitely the best game I have played recently. I highly recommend it. 10/10 game.

The more I play this game, the more addicted I get: You fail a run, upgrade your stats with the items you collected, start a new run and get farther than before. Because you're able to progress the story after every run, failing doesn't feel punishing. On the contrary: Dying is part of the gameplay loop and lets you progress in the game. 

When chosing between items in runs you have to decide if you wanna go for the ones that help you in just that run or if you wanna think long term and fail that run earlier in favor of getting farther the following runs. My advice is to not focus too much on one run but instead to look at the game as a continuos voyage. Enjoy the journey!

As a huge fan of greek mythology I absolutely adore the love they put into each and every character. Together with the beautiful art style this truly creates one of the most unique games I've ever played.

citations.review_text: Jogo bem feito, alguns momentos pode ser repetitivo, mas sabendo dozar é possivel apreciar. A arte, dublagem, trilha sonora e gameplay são boas. O unico ponto negativo é a pouca variedade de inimigos e puzzles (formas de avançar fazendo "quebra-cabeças" no cenário).

Seems to repetitive, kinda hard to progress. So basically you will grind for resources what you will spend for just a little better grind, for this it feels more like a idle clicker game than hack and slash

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features fixed boss encounters and rooms in a set order, leading to runs that can feel identical and repetitive over time.

citations.review_text:
[h2]METACRITIC SCORE -[/h2]  [h3]9.3/10[/h3]
[h2]MY ULTIMATE SCORE-[/h2]  [h3]9/10[/h3]

[h1]TLDR:[/h1]
[b]A very replay-able and fun game that is not too easy, but not too hard either.
With a touch of interesting narrative to keep you pushing towards the end, its addicting combat is all it really has, but with how fun and addicting that combat is, there is a reason why it is critically acclaimed.[/b] 


[h3]PROS:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Very engaging combat[/b] 
[*] [b]Rewarding progression[/b] 
[*] [b]Unique and cool setting- hell/hades[/b] 
[/list]


[h3]CONS:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]You will fight the same bosses and go through the same places over and over. They don't really "upgrade".[/b] 
[*] [b]You must rely on wiki or other sources to understand and pick the BEST choices. Game does not explain what symbols on doorways/rewards mean. You can learn on your own, but it will take longer than just having had a good guidebook/tutorial.[/b] 
[*] [b]You must successfully complete a run about 10 times to beat the game. Each time you do, the success is short lived, as you die from not being able to survive on earth, only in hades. This can feel like a cheap way for making you have to go through everything again, without any real reward besides some dialogue with a character.[/b] 
[/list]



[h1]NARRATIVE/STORY -[/h1]  [h3]8/10[/h3]
[b]This story is ultimately about patching things up between a father and son and mother.
It is told through dialogue, not through cutscenes.
Characters are well written, never feeling cheesy like some Nintendo games might (i do love Nintendo though!),
and they do have unique personalities.
This combination makes for a good time while having a real good reason to want to "escape hell", which is very intriguing.[/b] 



[h1]GAMEPLAY LOOP -[/h1]  [h3]10/10[/h3]
[b]Its just FUN. Addicting.
You also have variety, not only in what weapon you choose, but the "power-ups" that you choose throughout the game, so you can choose the playstyle that best suits yo…

Very good roguelite. Story is great voice acting is top notch, though it can get a little repetitive as runs as more or less identical with boss encounters being fixed and the chambers being in a set order. 

Highly recommend turning up the heat once you unlock it to keep it fresh while you finish the main story.

citations.review_text:
PROS
- One of the best roguelite gameplay loops ever made.
- Incredibly satisfying and responsive combat.
- Huge build variety with meaningful weapon differences.
- Excellent storytelling that naturally progresses through repeated runs.
- Memorable characters with outstanding voice acting.
- Beautiful art direction and fantastic soundtrack.
- Exceptional replay value.

CONS
- Some weapon aspects require a considerable amount of grinding to fully unlock.
- RNG can occasionally make certain builds difficult to assemble.

VERDICT
Hades is one of those rare games where I never minded failing. Every defeat still gave me something to look forward to, whether it was a new conversation, another character interaction, or an opportunity to try a completely different build. It perfectly balances addictive gameplay with meaningful storytelling, making each run feel worthwhile. Even after dozens of hours, I always found myself saying, "Just one more run." To me, Hades isn't just one of the best roguelites ever made, it's also one of the best indie games I've ever played.

5/5

Cool game. I loved the soundtrack, voice actors did a great job, nice visuals (hard to see enemies and understand what they're about to do at first, but one can get used to it), gameplay is pretty engaging with different weapons, movesets, boons and builds around these.
 
I'd say it's overhyped a bit, as it loses its pace a couple of times, and having finished the plot with so many things, like weapon aspects, untouched, not being able to give nectar to charcters 'coz of some weird limitation etc. etc. kinda made me feel betrayed, because I usually try to complete as many things in the game as I can before the finale, because after the finale I lose my motivation to play and never stay to wrap up the rest of the things, which in this case is A LOT of things.

Still, I'd sooner recommend to give this game a try than not. I don't regret playing it, I was consumed by this game most of the time, and there were many memorable moments, like the first victory over the final boss, but pacing and structure definitely would benefit from some revision.

I can see people falling in love with this game and 100% it, but I am not that guy. They say Hades II improved a lot of aspects, I will be giving that one a try for sure.

citations.review_text:
good roguelite, good story, good art, good music

The godhood option is very much needed (turn on if you want less damage taken, basically for beginners or anyone finding it too hard to beat the game). I like how the devs are very understanding in explaining this option, unlike other games where the player is mocked or achievements get locked if they turn on easy mode.

This was my first introduction to a roguelike game and I believe it was an amazing experience. My computer can handle it decently, but a smoother experience was obtained when I decreased the resolution. Especially when you add difficulty to your runs, things can get a bit overwhelming but the feeling of beating it is addicting. I'd say that luck in this game is handled really well, with items in the game reducing it a ton and making specific builds a lot easier to get which makes the game a lot more fun.

citations.review_text: 11/10 once u switch to controller and start sweating your face off, story artwork and such is stunning although the sex/romance innuendos get a bit wild lmao...

Holy crap, what a fun game!
I've played other roguelikes or roguelites, and many are fun, but you wouldn't think a strong story is one of their strengths.  In the case of Hades: story, voice acting, dialogue are all very strong points of the game.  And of course it's addictive and so damn fun!
  It's like instead of playing the same story over and over again at higher difficulties just for bragging rights, here it's playing the same run again and again actually advances the story.  I wouldn't have thought of making a game that way if i were going to make my own, but Hades pulls it off and then some.
  Oh yeah and it definitely plays better with a controller rather than mouse and keyboard I'd say, so if you have one then check this game out!

This roguelike captured my from start to finish.

The combat appears simple at first, but earn yourself a few modifiers ("boons" in this game) and that illusion will be quickly dispelled. Six weapons plus meta-upgrades that facilitate your ability to focus on a particular build means you get a uniquely customisable experience - do whatever worked well last time, or try to find a new favourite combo. All of this is built off a base that feels good enough on its own, but leaves space for all your boons to breathe - you can always optimise your playstyle for something.

Writing is pretty great. The story is somewhat one-note in terms of theme, but characters are pretty varied and realistic throughout. The game makes great use of its mythic setting - it doesn't under- or over-explain in my experience. It mostly leaves the "lore" to its source material (correct decision; the world is already established and there are too many games nowadays trying to get you to care about a setting devoid of character or a story that's actively hidden from you) but there are lots of clever references here and there to entertain fans of Greek Myth.

The game only falters somewhat in the later parts. Level 16 difficulty is reasonable, but I'm not grinding for level 32. Plus, enemies get so bulky and hit so hard with their dozens of different moves that it can start to frustrate a bit. Bosses are usually really fun, but can start to drag a bit if you don't have a damage-focused build.

Overall it's a pretty great game with a good story and fantastic sense of accomplishment waiting for you.

I love this game so much I decided to get every possible achievement. After more than 100 runs and getting the epilogue, it still had new lines of dialogues and contents! How crazy is that?
I really wish we could be able to play Hades but multiplayer :')

When people talk about video games as an art-form, this is what they are talking about. Fun and addictive gameplay loop with very satisfying meta-progression, but beyond that it's a truly beautiful story with so many loveable characters, incredibly grounded character development, and wonderful relationships with the player-character Zagreus and with each other.

There's so many unique pieces of dialogue that even after 100 hours, I could probably count the number of repeated interactions I heard on my fingers. Not the mention the astonishing visual art-style and literal artworks present in the game. 

The diversity in weapons, abilities, and accessories (Keepsakes, mostly) available to the player is amazing, particularly in how much thought and care went into each ones. That's not even mentioning the boons, the primary method of progression within each run, of which there are well over a hundred.

Greek Mythology is a well-trodden path for new media, especially in recent years, but I found that Hades does an incredible job bringing it to life. Each god (or other Mythological figure) has such a unique and vibrant design, wonderful voice acting, and the presence you would expect from their status.

Hades is well-deserving of all of the praise it's received over the years. Absolutely one of the best rogue-lite games in the genre.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the late-game requires an extensive number of repeated clears and resource grinding to fully advance the story and max relationships.

citations.review_text:
[i]Very Good; but I question its S-Tier Status[/i]

The difference between good and exceptional status in my opinion comes down to elements that can seem a bit nitpicky; but I think that is what holds Hades back from the highest accolades.

First, I’d like to highlight the strong points of the title. The mythology theming is great and is continuous throughout all facets of the game including the ever-present story dialogs. The art style is also very visually pleasing. Combat feel and control is generally very good, which is essential since that is what this game is about 90% of the time. Enemy attacks and intentions are fairly telegraphed in most instances. Six different weapon types to select from; each offering solid variety from one another and a ton of boon enhancements to alter the playstyle. Also, the game makes good use of long-term progression currency sinks to keep you coming back run after run to make little improvements. 

Now for some of the areas that I think could have been better. The game requires a ton of repeated clears to advance the story to the conclusion; likely far too many for most players. The last biome seems considerably less developed than the prior zones. The interior areas are generally extremely small and the main obstacle generally becomes ground damage from poison spills or hard to see projectiles. Although not often an issue there are still times that the amount of screen effects makes it extremely difficult to see what the enemies are trying to do. 

The story element delivery is hit and miss and can get pretty repetitive constantly talking to every NPC each run and listening to the excess banter. However, I think it does work when placed at the end of a successful run giving that little extra incentive to keep completing clears.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention an accessible 'God Mode' option in the settings that grants a toggleable damage resistance percentage that increases with each death.

citations.review_text:
just over 146 hours to get 100% achievements, I'm gonna be honest I was kind of taking my time with it but ah whatever here's an honest spoiler free review:

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]
I don't know what Supergiant was smoking but it is definitely not legal, in a good way.
The gameplay is absolutely the game's best selling point with a looootta f***ing build possibilities and all of them overload your eyes, ears and fingers with dopamine. You could study chemistry for years to create the perfect stimulant drug and implement it into a video game and it will STILL never be as good as the gameplay loop of Hades, I love love love love love [b] LOVE [/b] the gameplay. It is difficult but there is a 'god mode' which gives you damage resistance as you keep dying, there is no shame about using it as it can make the game less stressful, I personally left it on and I never felt overpowered,  things just felt more balanced for my experience. I'll spare the details because I could write a whole essay on just gameplay alone, this is one of the finest rougelikes on the market. + you can pet the giant puppy
[h1] Graphics [/h1]
The graphics of Hades are artistic with smooth animations for the majority of the game. It's a 2D ISO metric game with a unique and iconic style of its own which you can expect to fall in love with. The character designs are really nice and fitting for their characters with cool little details and it's a nice change of pace from how most media represents Greek mythology. And the weapons look cool
[h1] Music/sound design [/h1]
I like the mix of old/ancient Greek instruments being combined with synth, electric guitars and such. Each area has about 3-4 different tracks and there are other sections and situations with their own unique soundtracks which in the middle-late game you can LISTEN TO IN-GAME in the lobby area, it's a very nice addition. The soundtrack and the sound design in general has a wide range from goofy sound effects that play in dialogue to eargasm in …

This game has quickly become one of my favorites in recent years.

I love how the story unfolds through bite-sized character interactions, both mid-run & at the main hub. It's also kind of cool to see characters interacting with you & each other, based on your current/past actions, objectives, or equipment. Makes it feel dynamic & leads to some pretty hilarious moments, even in the Boss rooms.

Though it is my first rogue-lite experience, there's something uniquely satisfying about going through a run each time. It scratches that gaming itch, when you want something short and uncomplicated.

Auto-saving happens after every room, so the game's easy to pick up/put down.
Death never feels like a complete failure because room rewards balance between temporary run boosts and permanent resources used to unlock weapons, upgrades, and story progression.

Another nice feature is the "God Mode" option, in the settings.
You can toggle it on/off any time to grant you a 20% damage resistance.
If toggled on, it increases the damage resist by 2% with each death (capping at 80% total).
There's no penalty or missed content/achievements for having it on the entire time.
Great for if you want to ease into the difficulty & can be turned off without losing accumulated resistance progress.

The SFX/audio design is pretty good.
Everything from weapon usage to boon/item pickups feels unique and tactile.
Plus, the OST's metal tracks go hard AF, especially for the bosses.

Definitely a solid experience & well worth every minute.

[i]Very Good; but I question its S-Tier Status[/i]

The difference between good and exceptional status in my opinion comes down to elements that can seem a bit nitpicky; but I think that is what holds Hades back from the highest accolades.

First, I’d like to highlight the strong points of the title. The mythology theming is great and is continuous throughout all facets of the game including the ever-present story dialogs. The art style is also very visually pleasing. Combat feel and control is generally very good, which is essential since that is what this game is about 90% of the time. Enemy attacks and intentions are fairly telegraphed in most instances. Six different weapon types to select from; each offering solid variety from one another and a ton of boon enhancements to alter the playstyle. Also, the game makes good use of long-term progression currency sinks to keep you coming back run after run to make little improvements. 

Now for some of the areas that I think could have been better. The game requires a ton of repeated clears to advance the story to the conclusion; likely far too many for most players. The last biome seems considerably less developed than the prior zones. The interior areas are generally extremely small and the main obstacle generally becomes ground damage from poison spills or hard to see projectiles. Although not often an issue there are still times that the amount of screen effects makes it extremely difficult to see what the enemies are trying to do. 

The story element delivery is hit and miss and can get pretty repetitive constantly talking to every NPC each run and listening to the excess banter. However, I think it does work when placed at the end of a successful run giving that little extra incentive to keep completing clears.

“In the name of Hades…”

I initially bought Hades during a sale. I played until I managed to beat a run once, then it ended up sitting in my backlog. I figured that since it’s a roguelike, I could always come back to it whenever I wanted. Fast forward a year, and I finally found the time to properly play it. And oh boy, I missed out on a lot of fun.

Hades is the first roguelike I’ve ever played. I was already familiar with the genre since I’d seen countless reviews praising roguelikes for their insane replayability, and Hades is no exception. I don’t know if it was because I was burnt out from school or just tired of the games I had been playing, but once I started, I genuinely could not stop.

The premise alone immediately hooks you in. You play as Zagreus, battling your way out of the Underworld while trying to solve a whole lot of family problems along the way. The game’s four regions each have their own distinct atmosphere. There are also environmental hazards unique to each area, like the traps scattered throughout Tartarus or the pesky lava covering Asphodel. These hazards add another layer to the combat and constantly force you to stay alert. 

My favorite region is probably Elysium. I absolutely love its vibrant green scenery, and I appreciate that after entering a new region for the first time, the game gives you a moment to simply admire the environment before throwing you back into the action. From the scorching heat of Asphodel to the satyr-infested Temple of Styx, there’s never really a dull moment. Ironically, there were times I found myself wishing for one because of how relentlessly fast-paced the game is. Spotting Charon’s shop or finally stumbling upon a healing fountain after surviving several chambers always felt like a well-earned breather.

Speaking of surviving, the enemies in this game deserve their own paragraph.

Every single one of them has found a unique way to piss me off.
